description: Monophonic acid voice after the TB-303: oscillator, resonant lowpass filter, decay envelope, accent, slide and output stage, with a CV jack and attenuverter for each main control

params.text: Sets the reference tuning of the oscillator, 400Hz to 480Hz, separately from the pitch input
Sets the filter cutoff, about 314Hz to 2394Hz, on an exponential scale
Sets how far the decay envelope sweeps the filter, 0% to 100%, on a curve that puts most of the movement in the upper part of the travel until the taper is made linear on the menu
Sets the envelope decay on a logarithmic scale, 200ms to 2.5 seconds in the circuit model or about 460ms to 4.6 seconds in the Open303 model; an accented note uses the shortest time of that range
Sets how strongly an accented note is emphasised, 0% to 100%
Picks the oscillator waveform, sawtooth or square
Sets how much of the jack below it reaches the control above it: centre for none, clockwise for positive and anticlockwise for inverted, with ±5V covering the whole control at full depth

inputs.text: Pitch at a volt per octave, 0V giving C4; it is continuous unless the menu quantises it to semitones
Starts and ends notes, going high at 1V and staying high until it falls below 0.1V
Marks the note beginning as accented while it is at 1V or above, which changes loudness, filter movement and the accent envelope; the red lamp follows it

Requests a legato transition into the next note, on the same 1V and 0.1V thresholds as the gate; a gate falling while this is high keeps the voice alive for the next note, and the blue lamp follows it
A voltage modulating the control above it, at the depth and polarity its attenuverter sets

outputs.text: The voice output at a fixed full level, with no level control on the panel; it is clamped at ±12V, and accent and saturation can make it far hotter than an unaccented note

notes: an ATEK303 SEQ placed immediately to the left sends pitch, gate, accent and slide without cables; a cable in any of those four jacks replaces that one signal only.
each modulation jack starts with its attenuverter at the centre, so patching a cable does nothing until the small knob beside it is turned.
menu: Sound model: Circuit (ATEK), Open303 original — picks a whole group of oscillator, filter, decay, saturation and slide settings at once; Custom shows when they match neither
Motor — under Fine tuning, picks the oscillator, either Open303's wavetables or the model taken from the schematic
Pulse width (TM5) — under Fine tuning, the width of the square wave, 44% through 56%
Square droop — under Fine tuning, how far the square wave tilts across each cycle, from none to 60Hz
Saw: reset corner — under Fine tuning, how hard the sawtooth's reset is, 1 microsecond sharp through 20 microseconds round
Saw droop — under Fine tuning, how far the sawtooth tilts, 0.7Hz through 15Hz
Motor — under Fine tuning, picks the filter, either Open303's or a diode ladder model
Linear resonance (VR4 linear pot) — under Fine tuning, makes the resonance knob follow the circuit's linear law rather than Open303's curve
Drive — under Fine tuning, how hard the signal hits the filter, 0dB, 6dB or 12dB
Decay range — under Fine tuning, what the decay knob covers, Open303's 460ms to 4.6 seconds or the circuit's 200ms to 2.5 seconds
Accent accumulation (C72 network) — under Fine tuning, lets closely spaced accents build on each other and carry into the notes that follow
Accent stages — under Fine tuning, which accent envelopes are used: the fast 100ms one, the slow 450ms one, or both as the circuit has them
Log Env Mod taper (VR5 audio pot) — under Fine tuning, gives the envelope amount knob an audio taper; turning it off makes the knob and its CV linear
Slide in semitones/s (as the circuit) — under Fine tuning, glides in pitch rather than in frequency, which keeps the rate even across the range
Slide τ — under Fine tuning, the time constant of the glide, 60ms, 120ms or 220ms
Quantize pitch to semitones — under Fine tuning, rounds the incoming pitch to chromatic semitones
Limit to the 303 range (C1–C4) — under Fine tuning, clamps the note range to the original three octaves; without quantisation a fractional semitone can carry slightly past those bounds
Auto-legato (slide without SLIDE input) — under Fine tuning, starts a glide when the pitch changes under a held gate; off by default, so a moving CV does not glide by accident
OTA saturation (BA662A, before the VCA) — under Fine tuning, None, Soft or Hard saturation ahead of the amplifier
Output saturation (mixer + LA4140) — under Fine tuning, None, Soft or Hard saturation in the final output path
Analogue drift (R-2R DAC + posistor) — under Fine tuning, how much the tuning and cutoff wander: None, Subtle, Marked or Heavy, the menu giving the cents and per cent for each
Unit (DAC error pattern) — under Fine tuning, picks one of four repeatable note-by-note tuning error patterns, which does not change from note to note
